commissioning_notice: U-K1 INSTRUMENT -- COMMISSIONED ON eval.k1.COMMISSIONED_SETS ONLY. All three commissioning constructions (must-accept, must-reject 1, must-reject 2) fire correctly and readings are load-bearing on: SciFact, NFCorpus, FiQA-2018, ArguAna (D-SLM4707, 2026-08-25, instrument commit 3426bee; the zero-qrels guard's vitality proven on these four) and SCIDOCS (D-SLM5363, 2026-08-30, on a content-distance-aware remedy construction for must-reject 2, after a first attempt -- D-SLM5338 -- returned NOT COMMISSIONED on the original construction). See eval.k1.COMMISSIONING_DECISIONS for the decision ID governing each set. NOTE ON SCIDOCS: its must-reject-1 construction fires by a narrow margin -- exceeds its own resolving power by roughly 3e-05, a genuine boundary case independently measured twice, corroborated across three seeds, non-replicating at two alternate dimensions, and independently backed by an F2 floor rejection at roughly 11x its own resolving power regardless. A construction that fires does not retroactively validate a different, unexecuted configuration (commissioning spec Section 5): any other locked set -- present in eval.k1.set_roster.ALL_LOCKED_SETS but absent from eval.k1.COMMISSIONED_SETS -- has never had its own must-accept/must-reject constructions fired, and its readings stay quarantined (recorded, never acted on, never headlined, not read into any gate verdict as load-bearing) until an independent seat runs them and files the executed verdict as a decision-log entry citing the commissioning spec. Readings are ALSO subject to the design's own component re-commissioning rule, which is a separate condition: any subsequent change to the loader, ranker, scorer, or guard requires the constructions it touches to be re-fired, on every set they touch, before a new reading from the changed code is trusted (Claude/Mendeleev/u-k1-commissioning-execution3-2026-08-25.md, Claude/Mendeleev/te46-scidocs-mustreject2-remedy-2026-08-30.md, and Claude/Mendeleev/u-k1-commissioning-2026-08-25.md Section 5, Wizard project records tree). RE-COMMISSIONING CURRENTLY OUTSTANDING (TE-51 H-2): b16ac70 (TE-50, 2026-08-30) changed four commissioned components -- bm25_baseline._tokenize (the BM25 analyzer), embed_runner (the reference's query vectors), rank_score (the paired resolving power dispersion) and gate.evaluate_f2 (the verdict arithmetic) -- after every set in eval.k1.COMMISSIONED_SETS already had its own COMMISSIONED verdict filed. D-SLM5396 records the gap; D-SLM5397 defers it, explicitly 'before K1-Run-2's verdict is read as load-bearing.' No reading this instrument has produced from b16ac70 forward has been re-commissioned against the changed code (Claude/Poirot/b16ac70-te51-k1-instrument-confirmation.md Finding H-2, Wizard project records tree).

self_exclusion_convention: Self-exclusion convention: a candidate document whose id equals the ranking query's own id is dropped from the ranked list before truncation to k (BEIR's ignore_identical_ids=True, on by default in beir/retrieval/evaluation.py, which is the convention every published anchor read against this instrument was itself produced under). This fires only on sets where a query id can also name a corpus document (ArguAna today); it is a no-op everywhere else, verified by executed check. Implemented once, in eval.k1.self_exclusion.exclude_self_and_truncate, and applied uniformly by every ranker in this package (the dense ranker and the BM25 baseline) -- U-K1 fix round 2 (D-SLM4699) fixed the dense ranker; fix round 2b (D-SLM4699 class fix) extracted the shared helper so the BM25 baseline, which carried the identical defect, is fixed by the same code rather than a second, independently-written copy.
